text:
Minnesota did most of its winning in the first period, and the numbers say it earned the lead rather than stumbled into it. Matt Boldy opened the scoring at 11:50, Maxim Shabanov cashed in on the game's only power play at 14:32 (a 4 percent chance, so a bit of a bonus), and Danila Yurov made it 3-0 at 16:57. Vegas had given up three goals in about five minutes on a first period that was close on chance quality (MIN 1.23 expected goals, VGK 1.10).

After that, the Wild controlled the middle of the game. They outchanced Vegas 1.40 to 0.37 in the second, and Rasmus Andersson's slap shot at 2:37, a 3 percent look, was the only thing the Golden Knights had to show for it. Jesper Wallstedt faced 23 shots and stopped 21 of them, a touch better than the 2.75 goals the shots were worth. William Karlsson cut it to 3-2 at 9:25 of the third, and Vegas pushed to 1.27 expected goals in that period, but Minnesota's lead held.

Joel Eriksson Ek sealed it at 18:38 with a wrist shot that had a 52 percent chance of going in, set up by Kirill Kaprizov. Minnesota finished with 4.27 expected goals to Vegas's 2.75, and simulated replays of every shot give the Wild the win 62 percent of the time. That makes 4-2 a fair reflection of the game, with the Wild a little more efficient than they strictly needed to be. Vegas took 15 penalty minutes to Minnesota's 7 and never found a way to turn the third-period push into a tie.
